target_customer: Contractors with $100M+ revenue, especially those building data centers, who run large equipment fleets
problem: Contractors coordinate equipment repairs, idle machines and invoices by phone and spreadsheet, so downtime and unaudited repair bills eat into fixed price margins.
business_model: Enterprise software sold annually upfront, with an AI operator (Adam) for equipment operations; sells no parts, rentals or machines
product_category: AI operations workspace for construction equipment and fleets

founders.name: Muhammad Alasgarli
education: Washington University in St. Louis, dual BS in Computer Science and Finance (3 years)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built ML software for Hunter Engineering in college that it credits with $100M+ in sales; this is self-reported.

founders.name: Suleyman Alasgarli
prior_employers: Regional dental services group (grew it from $5M to $21M in 20 months, per YC page)
education: UMKC, BA in Biology through the six-year BA/MD program; left medical school to build Carma
previous_startups: Slabkick (online graded card marketplace, 10,000+ users, outcome not stated)

technical_complexity.rationale: At founding the product was a fleet and auto repair coordination marketplace and software, mostly standard engineering. The later agentic operator needs integrations with contractor systems, invoice auditing and cost modeling, which is moderately hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Value comes from workflow integration and customer data once embedded at enterprise contractors, but the AI layer itself could be copied by telematics and fleet software vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Fleetio and Samsara added AI maintenance features in 2026 per press coverage found, but no acquisition or direct copy of the construction operator wedge was found.

market_need_then: The company's own pitch cites late data center projects and contractors working at fixed prices, so idle crews and broken machines come straight out of margin. These are company claims, not independently verified.

branding.domain_note: Site is joincarma.com, not carma.com, suggesting the exact .com was unavailable; no source on how the domain was chosen.

identity.mascot_or_character: Adam, the named AI operator, is the product persona
identity.voice_and_tone: Profit focused and patriotic framing in the YC description, with a claim that Carma sells no parts so its incentive is the customer's profit

brand_strength.rationale: Search found no press about the brand itself and several unrelated companies named Carma, so the name is confusable. The Adam persona is the only distinct asset.

pivots.from: Marketplace and software for auto repair and fleet maintenance
pivots.to: Agentic workspace for construction equipment operations
pivots.why: Not stated in sources found; the YC page and site describe the earlier fleet focus as rebuilt.

outcome_analysis: Carma is active and early. It started in W24 as a fleet and auto repair product, then refocused on construction equipment operations for large contractors, where it claims $2M ARR three months after its first invoice with five customers. These figures are self-reported. No funding announcement could be verified, so the capital position is unknown, and no shutdown or acquisition was found.
notes: Aggregators (Altss, SeedTable, roundfunded) report a $5.5M seed backed by Soma Capital, Y Combinator and the Superhuman founders, and a $500K pre-seed in Feb 2024; none was confirmed by a primary announcement or a second outlet, so these are unverified and not recorded as rounds. CB Insights lists a different New Jersey company named Carma Technology; ignored. No dated competitors near Jan 2024 were found; the search returned only 2026 coverage of Fleetio and Samsara AI features, which is not as of founding. No outcome news found beyond YC status Active. Completeness pass: Rounds rest on aggregators only (Seedtable seed, Altss pre-seed); no primary announcement found, seed date not given.
